newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end firmer, helped by NY, chip data.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end firmer, helped by NY, chip data.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended on a firm note on Tuesday, cheered on by the bull run on Wall Street and strong U.S. semiconductor data, brokers said. They added that the market was also supported psychologically by signs that the domestic economy was not really as feeble as thought by some.
At the day's end, the key Nikkei 225 stood at 21,206.43, up 141.35 points, or 0.67 percent. Its December futures climbed 100 points to 21,200.
"There was fierce resistance at the 21,300 level, capping gains, but major issues headed by chip makers were well sought after," said Kenzo Doi, Kokusai Securities strategist.
Mitsubishi Oil on the other hand sank to a new yearly low of 802 yen after losing nine, unable to shrug off the after-effects of last week's raid on the company's headquarters by Tokyo prosecutors.
Brokers said that despite renewed strength in the benchmark, rises in other indices were small in comparison.

The broader TOPIX was 3.92 points or 0.25 percent higher at 1,576.75. The Nikkei 300 was 0.82 points or 0.28 percent up at 295.90. The second section index edged 0.04 point higher to 2,034.89 in a turnover of 14.02 million. That compares to 14.7 million on Monday.

Language school Nova Corp made its debut at a price of 6,150 yen in the over-the-counter (OTC) market, contrary to hopes that it would be around the 6,500 level, brokers said. The public offer price was 5,460 yen.
The OTC index was 2.48 points or 0.17 percent lower at 1,465.12 in late trade.
